transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having more trouble keeping my mind on things than I used to. It’s probably not anything dramatic, but at work I’ll be looking at a loan worksheet or a follow-up list and realize I’ve read the same line several times and still haven’t really taken it in.

Then I end up putting off calls or small decisions because they feel harder than they should. I don’t know if I’m explaining that right, but it’s been bothering me.
Have you noticed any loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy, like hobbies, work tasks, or spending time with family and friends?

Yes… I mean, I still do those things. I still go to the community center, and I keep up with my garden. So it’s not like I’ve completely stopped, if that makes sense.

But most days there’s this kind of dull heaviness with me. Even in places that used to really lift me up, I feel like I’m more just going through the motions… smiling and acting normal, I guess. It’s probably not as bad as some people have it, but yes, I have noticed that.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the time, almost every day, even when there's no clear reason for it?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I still get up and do what I’m supposed to do. But most days there’s this dull heaviness sitting with me.

Even when I’m at the community center or out in my garden—places that used to lift me up—I’m there, but I feel like I’m just going through the motions with a smile pasted on. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed feeling fatigued or having low energy most days, even after getting enough rest?

Yes… I suppose I have. I don’t want to overstate it, because I am sleeping and I’m still getting things done.

But a lot of mornings I wake up already tired, even if I’ve had a full night. And then after just a couple of client calls, or even something simple like watering the tomatoes, my body feels like I’ve already put in a whole day. It feels a little silly saying it that way, but that’s how it’s been.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual or that your thoughts feel slowed down?

Not so much that I’m physically moving slowly, I don’t think… or at least I haven’t noticed that in a big way.

But my thoughts, yes. That’s actually part of why I came in. I just can’t seem to keep my mind on things like I used to. I’ll be looking at a loan worksheet or a client follow-up list, and I’ll reread the same line over and over like it just isn’t sinking in.

And then I put off making calls sometimes, not because I don’t care, but because even simple decisions feel harder than they should. I know that probably sounds small, but it’s been bothering me.

Have you been having trouble sleeping—like not being able to fall asleep, waking up during the night, or waking up earlier than you should—or on the flip side, have you found yourself sleeping much more than usual?

I’m not sure I’d say my sleep is a major problem, honestly. I mean, I go to bed and I do sleep.

Some nights I might wake up or feel like it wasn’t the most restful, but I haven’t really been keeping track, and I don’t know that it’s more than normal for someone my age. And I’m not sleeping all day or anything like that.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

I don’t think so… nothing that I’ve really noticed, anyway.

My appetite seems about the same, and my clothes fit about the same, so I don’t think there’s been any real weight change. I mean, I don’t weigh myself constantly, but nothing has stood out to me. Does that answer it okay?
How long have you been feeling this way — this heaviness, trouble focusing, and low energy — have these been happening for at least a couple of weeks, or longer?

It’s been longer than a couple of weeks, yes.

I guess I’ve been trying not to make too much of it, but it really started after my close friend died… a little over two years ago now. I kept thinking it would lift with time, and some days are better than others, but that heaviness and the trouble focusing have kind of stuck around.

Is that the kind of timeline you mean?

Since the time your friend passed away over two years ago, have there been any periods lasting at least a few weeks where you felt like you were back to your usual self — where the heaviness and trouble focusing eased up significantly?

I don’t think there’s been a stretch of a few weeks where I felt completely back to myself, no.

I mean, I’ve had better days, and times when I could sort of push through and seem okay, but since my friend died a little over two years ago, it’s been… kind of there in the background most of the time. I kept hoping it was just taking a while. Is that what you’re asking?
Have these feelings of heaviness and trouble focusing made it harder for you to function at work or in your daily life, even if you’re still managing to get things done?

Yes… I think it has, though I’m still getting by.

At work, at the credit office, I’ve started putting off some client follow-ups, which isn’t really like me. I do get to them eventually, but it takes more effort than it should.

And outside of work, I’ve kind of stepped back from things I used to make a point of doing, like gallery events and the walking-club outings. I tell myself I’m just tired or busy, but… I guess it has affected my day-to-day life some. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
